newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on weaker sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on weaker sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B Shares closed down on Thursday on weak market sentiment following the recent falls due to poor interim results, brokers said.
The index dipped 0.140 points or 0.27 percent to 51.191 points, on volume of 8.6 million shares worth $2.7 million. Of 41 B shares, 32 traded with 16 down, six flat and 10 up.
Brokers said that consecutive falling in the past few days, mainly caused by poor interim results, had depressed the market sentiment so much that the index would fall further in the short term.
"Domestic institutional buying in selective stocks failed to support the market, because overseas selling was heavier," one broker said.
"But the index will find support at 50 points," a second broker said.
China First Pencil performed the worst, falling $0.012 or 3.79 percent to $0.304 on volume of 90,000 shares.
Shanghai Steel Tube traded the most on overseas institutional selling, slipping $0.002 or 1.63 percent to $0.120 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai A share index ended up but off an intra-day high of 878.094 points on heavy profit-taking later in the session, brokers said.
The index gained 2.606 points or 0.31 percent to 852.083 points, on volume of 622.4 million shares worth 5.7 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 index put on 6.976 points or 0.32 percent to 2189.446 points.
North-east Hualian was the star, surging 0.42 yuan or 12.06 percent to 3.90 yuan on volume of 25.2 million shares.
